stimuli.description: Virtual office spaces with 4 different visual layouts (Office A, B, C, D), each with 2 window views (good and bad urban views).
stimuli.source: Section 2.3 Visual stimuli generation using VR technology, Fig. 5

stimuli.description: Three levels of speech sound pressure level (Lp,A,S,4m: low 45.9 dB, middle 51.1 dB, high 55.9 dB) combined with fixed background noise (47.0 dB).

tables.description: Acoustic parameters (Lp,A,S,4m, D2,s, rD, RT30, D50) from field measurements and computer simulations for different sound conditions (Low, Middle, High).
Visual characteristics of different OPO layouts (Office A, B, C, D) including Window area ratio, W/L, Floor area, Capacity, and Floor area per person.
Spearman correlation coefficients (rs) between physical parameters (acoustic and visual) and perceived affective quality attributes (Loud, Variable, Reverberant, Bright, Orderly, Wide).

Spearman correlation coefficients (rs) between physical parameters (acoustic and visual) and overall quality indicators (Acoustic satisfaction, Visual satisfaction, Speech privacy, Visual privacy, Work satisfaction, Task performance).

Spearman correlation coefficients (rs) between perceived affective quality attributes (Loud, Variable, Reverberant, Bright, Orderly, Wide) and overall quality indicators (Acoustic satisfaction, Visual satisfaction, Speech privacy, Visual privacy, Work satisfaction, Task performance).

limitations: Only subjects in their 20s participated, limiting generalizability.
Normality was not achieved for survey results.
Only visual and audio stimuli in a limited office space were used, limiting cognitive model clarity.
Lack of gender balance in recruited subjects.
Task performance quantified only with digit span test, not various cognitive skills.
Short-term stimuli used, not considering long-term effects (fatigue, stress).
Audio-visual attributes selected through a small focus group interview, not representing general OPO soundscape.
Evaluation scale for indoor soundscape needs further study.
Limited to visual and auditory senses, not considering other indoor environmental quality factors (air, thermal).
Only male sound sources used, not considering female voices with different fundamental frequencies.
Further research needed for individual worker characteristics (sensitivity, work satisfaction, career, gender, education, economic level).
